page: Amazon Web Services m9g.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the instance achieving top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core testing. It also demonstrates strong memory performance, scoring 2799.13 in the PassMark memory test, and average performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling represent a notable tradeoff; multi-core benchmarks, such as the Geekbench multi-core score and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, fall into the weaker percentiles due to the low core count.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.large offers a modern ARMv9 architecture that delivers high single-threaded efficiency and strong memory performance relative to its resource footprint. This makes it highly suitable for workloads that do not require massive parallelization but benefit from high single-core clock speeds and memory throughput. Recommended workloads include lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, text processing, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose utility applications.

This instance is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring strong single-threaded execution and moderate memory, making it well-suited for lightweight web serving, text processing, and caching applications.
